_note: The catalog scripts/seed_store.py creates on an empty store, so a freshly provisioned store shows every read and alert this example implements. Handles and product types line up with data/thresholds.json: the low-stock rules there are keyed on 'Workshop tools', 'Storage', and the canvas-tool-apron handle, and the quantities below are chosen to sit on either side of them. The products are the same ones the test fixture describes, so a live store and the suite tell the same story.

products.title: Canvas tool apron
products.description: Waxed canvas, six pockets, riveted at every seam. The apron most of the bench crew ends up wearing.
products.seo_description: A waxed canvas apron with six pockets, built for the workshop bench.
products._why: The ordinary case: one variant, a unit cost, healthy stock. Every margin and pricing read has something to work with.

products.title: Folding step stool
products.description: Two heights, folds flat against a wall. Powder-coated steel with a textured tread.
products.seo_description: A folding steel step stool in two heights.
products._why: A variant ladder. A price move has to scale the whole ladder rather than flatten it to one price, and the catalog read has to report a range.

products.title: Bench dog set
products._why: Low stock against the 'Workshop tools' threshold of 12, and thin content: a four-word description, no SEO description, and no images. The content-quality read should call it poor.

products.title: Shop stool cushion
products.description: A firm foam cushion with a canvas cover, sized to the shop stool.
products.seo_description: A canvas-covered cushion for the ACME shop stool.
products._why: A draft, which the merchant interface reads as paused and not visible in the storefront. Plenty of stock, so it also reads as a slow mover.

products.title: Layout square
products.description: Machined aluminium, etched to a quarter inch, square enough to check other squares against.
products.seo_description: A machined aluminium layout square etched to a quarter inch.
products._why: No unit cost. Every margin figure must be absent rather than guessed, and the price floor falls back to the guardrail rather than to cost.

products.title: Sawdust broom
products.description: Horsehair over a turned ash handle, stiff enough for a swept concrete floor.
products.seo_description: A horsehair broom with a turned ash handle.
products._why: Inventory is not tracked. It raises no stock alert and cannot be restocked, which is a refusal the assistant has to explain rather than a failure.

products.title: Cast iron hold-down
products.description: Cast and machined in one piece, with a cam that grips at any bench thickness up to three inches.
products.seo_description: A cast iron bench hold-down with a cam clamp.
products._why: Plenty of stock and almost no sales: the clearest slow mover in the catalog.

products.title: Discontinued mallet
products.description: A rawhide mallet the shop no longer stocks.
products._why: Archived. It must not appear in the catalog, in any alert, or as a listing the assistant can change; a live store proves that as well as the suite does.

_orders_note: The Admin API cannot backdate an order: draftOrderComplete stamps the order with the time it ran, and it will not create a refund for the asking. scripts/seed_store.py therefore reads only each order's lines, which means a freshly seeded store has sales in the current period and none in the period before it, and no refunds at all; the snapshot reads as a rise from zero until the store has been running a fortnight, and the return-spike rule stays quiet. Nothing in this example papers over that — the assistant reports the window it actually measured. The local store (SHOPIFY_LOCAL_STORE=1) is not bound by either limit, so it honours days_ago, fulfillment, and refunded below, and api/local_store.py invents further history behind them.

orders._why: The store's ordinary traffic: the apron and the step stool are what sells.
Nine units of the bench dog set across two orders, against stock of two: what puts it over its low-stock threshold and keeps it out of the slow-mover list.
One layout square, so the no-unit-cost product has sales but not enough to leave the slow-mover list.
Left unfulfilled on purpose. It is not a delayed order yet — the fulfilment window is three days — and it becomes one if the store sits untouched for a long weekend.

Unfulfilled and older than the fulfilment window, so the order-issues read has a delayed order to find. On a real store this one starts inside the window and crosses out of it as the store sits; locally it is already outside.
